chunks.heading: CapitalLens documentation
chunks.text: CapitalLens is a portfolio dashboard for Trading 212 investors: positions, pies, analyst views, strategy and profit-booking guidance, returns, a watchlist with IPO Watch, and an alert inbox. This is the complete product documentation. It lives in git next to the code (documentation/), is published as this portal (/help/) and is linked from the footer of every dashboard.

chunks.heading: How this documentation is kept true
chunks.text: - It is in git and changes in the same commit as the feature (standing rule in CLAUDE.md). - The table, workflow and menu references are generated from the code , so they cannot drift. - tests/standards test.py fails the build if a menu has no page, a page is missing from the portal, the generated pages are stale, or a dashboard lacks the footer link. - Every dashboard footer links here: 📘 Documentation . Honest-data rule: where a number cannot be verified the app says so. These pages name the source of every figure and call out what is estimated.

chunks.title: Product overview
chunks.heading: What it is
chunks.text: CapitalLens turns a Trading 212 account into a decision dashboard: where the money is, how it is performing, what the data says about each holding, and when to buy, hold, trim or review. It is built phone-first and shows its working: every figure names its source, and anything that cannot be verified is labelled rather than guessed.

chunks.title: Product overview
chunks.heading: Who it is for
chunks.text: Self-directed Trading 212 investors who use pies and want one place for allocation, performance, alerts and a weekly plan. The product is heading to a public multi-user service: self-service sign-up, Trading 212 connected first (Zerodha later) by read-only API key, and a demo user with mock data. Today one real user (the owner) and the demo user are testing.

chunks.title: Product overview
chunks.heading: Investing approach it supports
chunks.text: - Base-case growth about 10% a year , optimistic 15% . - Aggressive mode: the monthly maximum budget is paid in weekly across pies, weighted by performance, market fear and news. Weightings are calibrated to a recurring £30 contribution on the Trading 212 pies (Defence, Atomic Resources, Cloud Empire, speculative tech, emerging markets). - Dip alerts, when to sell or buy more, rebalancing advice, and phone notifications. These are screening aids and rule-based estimates, not financial advice .

chunks.title: Product overview
chunks.heading: Principles
chunks.text: 1. Zero knowledge: the server never sees plaintext holdings; per-user data is encrypted in the browser. Only public data (instruments, market cache, IPO calendar) is shared. See Architecture & security. 2. Honest data: no fake "all clear"; ratings and prices carry their source; missing data is said to be missing. 3. Mobile first: every section fits 360px and 390px with no sideways scroll; tap targets are at least 40px. 4. Everything collapses, and the open/closed state is remembered per user. 5. One rollout: a feature reaches every dashboard variant, built from the same sources. 6. Nothing runs while the app is closed: the owner opens the app each morning and presses Refresh; sync, alerts and phone push happen then.

chunks.title: 🔔 Alerts
chunks.heading: Market signals: Live · Pre Market · Post Market
chunks.text: - 🌤️ Pre Market : what was already true at today's open = the last completed daily close before today's session. - 🌙 Post Market : today's completed session, once that market has closed. Honest about data: the signals are computed from Yahoo daily closes (one year) fetched when you open the tab , with up to 5 fetches in parallel, cached for 10 minutes, Rescan at the bottom. It is not a real-time feed and nothing is pushed while the app is closed . A 100-day cross needs 101+ sessions, a 200-day cross 201+, a 52-week high 200+ prior sessions; a stock with less history simply gets no such signal. A stock whose chart cannot be read is listed as "could not be read" , never shown as clear. Empty views say why (e.g. no market open right now). A screening aid, not advice. Code: engine and cards docs/js/signals.js (analyse, scan, group, html); tabs, scan wiring and Inbox in docs/js/alerts.js; the scan starts only once the Alerts tab is open (alertsShown() from the router). The demo serves its stored mock 1-year charts through demo-shim.js.

chunks.title: 🔔 Alerts
chunks.heading: Alerts are review reports
chunks.text: One house style for every alert (dashboard, phone push, email). Each report contains: 1. Holding weight vs strategic target , with the difference. 2. Threshold check: latest GBP price, daily change, 20-day closing high, drawdown. 3. A review flag. 4. A data-coverage note saying what could and could not be checked. No alert and no "clear" status is produced for a holding whose data cannot be verified ; the report says so instead.

chunks.title: 🔔 Alerts
chunks.heading: Support-zone alerts (private app, issue #51)
chunks.text: Raised on the morning Refresh (nothing runs while the app is closed) for stocks you hold that have a level in support levels (see Strategy › Support Levels). Type support, in the same review-report style: live price, the zone, distance, your average cost, the source and capture date , a review flag, and "an external view, not our calculation". - Transitions only: 🛡️ reached its support zone (from above or approaching; default priority) and 🔻 below its support zone (high priority). The first time a stock is seen its status is only recorded, so stocks already in or below a zone do not flood the inbox. Back above or reclaiming the zone raises nothing. The same alert is not repeated within 24 hours. - Honest about data: the Trading 212 quote currency must equal the zone's currency; if it is unknown or different, nothing is compared and no alert is raised. - Code: analyse() in docs/zk/monitor.js (levels passed in by docs/zkapp/zkapp-tools.js / docs/zk/zk.js); status stored in the encrypted monitor state (support status). Test: tests/zk support alert test.mjs.

chunks.heading: ❓ Help assistant
chunks.text: Question it answers: how do I use CapitalLens? A small AI assistant answers how-to and documentation questions from these help pages and links to the page it used. Epic 54 on GitHub.

chunks.title: ❓ Help assistant
chunks.heading: Where it is
chunks.text: A round ❓ button at the bottom-left of every dashboard (legacy, demo, private app and its production build; docs/js/helpbot.js). It only shows while you are signed in. Tap it to open a chat sheet, type a question, read the answer and tap a source link to open the exact help page. Clear empties the chat and ✕ closes it. The chat lives in the browser only and is wiped when you sign out. It works with whichever sign-in the dashboard uses: the Supabase session of the private app / demo (both projects), or the legacy dashboard's own session (checked through capitallens-proxy /session/check).

chunks.title: ❓ Help assistant
chunks.heading: What it does
chunks.text: - You type a question about how CapitalLens works ("How do I turn on the live feed?", "What is the Dip Planner?"). - It finds the matching help sections and writes a short answer from them, with up to three links to the exact page. - If the help pages do not cover the question it says so and points to the Documentation. It does not guess.

chunks.title: ❓ Help assistant
chunks.heading: What it never does
chunks.text: - No financial advice. It will not say what to buy or sell, or where a price is going. It can explain how the Dip Planner and Strategy tab read their signals; you decide the amount and the trade. - No access to your portfolio. It only sees the question you type. It never receives holdings, encrypted data, keys or Trading 212 credentials, and CapitalLens stays zero-knowledge. - No secrets. A message that looks like an API key, password or card number is refused before it is sent anywhere. - No internals. It only knows the user-facing pages (home, product overview, one page per menu). Security, architecture, operations, engineering and database pages are never indexed.

chunks.title: 📊 Overview
chunks.heading: Market decline by country (card)
chunks.text: A collapsible card with 1D / 1W / 1M / 3M / 6M / 9M / 1Y buttons and one horizontal bar per country (red for a decline, green for a gain, worst first). It is your holdings by country , not index data: each holding's price change between the latest saved snapshot and an older one, weighted by its value at the start. Funds are split by their country weights (instrument country weights); holdings with no country data are grouped as Unclassified , never hidden. A holding with no price at both dates is left out. A span longer than the saved history says "not enough saved history yet" instead of showing a made-up bar. The older snapshot is the newest one that is at least about 80% of the span old, and its date is shown. Source: the portfolio snapshots and positions tables. Guarded by tests/zk overview stale test.mjs.

chunks.title: 📊 Overview
chunks.heading: Investments value over time (card)
chunks.text: A collapsible line chart with 1D / 1W / 1M / 3M / 6M / 9M / 1Y buttons, like the Trading 212 home screen. Each point is a saved snapshot's investments value as Trading 212 defines it (cost basis + unrealised result, from the snapshot's account data). Snapshots saved before that data was kept are left out so the line never mixes two definitions; the card says how many points it has and how many days they cover, and draws no line with fewer than two points. The change shown is first to last point in the span, and the card notes that buying or selling moves the value, so a rise is not always performance. Points exist only for days you pressed Refresh ("nothing runs while the app is closed"), so it is sparser than Trading 212's own chart. Source: portfolio snapshots. Guarded by tests/zk overview stale test.mjs and tests/zk invest line test.mjs. How the line is drawn (so a small move never looks like a crash): - The vertical axis has labelled min / mid / max lines in pounds and is never tighter than 2% of the value : a £45 move on £4,800 stays a wobble, not a cliff.

chunks.title: 📊 Overview
chunks.heading: Investments value over time (card)
chunks.text: The start and end of the span are labelled underneath (times for a day, dates for longer). - Every snapshot is a dot (the latest is larger). A gap with no snapshots (overnight, or the app was not refreshed) is drawn dashed , never as a steep solid slope. - A change in cost basis of £5 or more (and 0.2%) is marked ▲ buy / ▼ sell with a dotted line, because buying or selling moves the line without being performance. Under the figure the card splits the change into cost basis (buys/sells) and unrealised result ; both are Trading 212's own figures. Rebuilt history (below) has no cost basis, so it shows no markers. - Touch or hover the chart to read a point: time, investments value, cost basis, unrealised result and, on a marker, the buy/sell amount.

Sells are matched oldest buy first (FIFO) ; a stock you have sold completely, or that sits only inside pies, is not listed . Stocks are sorted by £ gain. chunks.title: 💰 Profit Booking & Capital Protection
chunks.heading: Live data architecture
chunks.text: pbFetchPtsOrdered(sym) — POST to PROXY/chart with {symbol, range:'1y'}. Returns sorted array of daily closes. No server-side KV cache (Cloudflare does not cache POST requests). pbComputeRegimeLive(storedBreadth) — always fetches ^GSPC, ACWI, ^VIX in parallel (never reuses ovMk, which may be hours old). 15-min client-side result cache pbLiveRegCache. pbPatchLiveHoldingDMAs(rows) — iterates rows, groups unique yahoo ticker values, batch-fetches 4 at a time, patches id="pb-dma-{sym}" spans in-place. 15-min per-symbol client cache pbDmaCache.

Future improvement: derive live breadth from pbDmaCache once it populates.

chunks.title: ⚙ Settings & account
chunks.heading: Connecting Trading 212 (step by step)
chunks.text: 1. In Trading 212: Settings → API , create a key with read-only permissions (never one that can trade). 2. Open ⚙ Settings → Refresh your data (or the account page's sync box). 3. Paste the key and secret; press Refresh now . It syncs, re-analyses and turns the live feed on (one button): the headline numbers (total value, P&L, cash) then update every 5 minutes while the tab stays open. The key is never sent to or stored in the database or localStorage. A page reload does not switch live off: while you stay signed in, the key is kept in this tab's sessionStorage, encrypted under your data key (never plaintext), and the live feed resumes by itself after a reload with no re-entry. It is removed when you log out , on the 45-minute inactivity logout , when you press ⏹ Stop live feed , or when the tab/browser closes (then you sign in and press Refresh now again). Guarded by tests/zk live persist test.mjs. A ⏹ Stop live feed button appears while live; there is no separate Start button. The automatic re-analysis at login never starts the feed (it has no key).

chunks.heading: Connecting Trading 212 (step by step)

chunks.title: ⚙ Settings & account
chunks.heading: What the refresh tells you (issue #53)
chunks.text: After every refresh a box under the button lists, in plain words: - What changed : "Portfolio snapshot saved: 33 positions", "New positions: …", "Quantity changed: AAAl 10 → 12", "No longer held: …", "New orders from Trading 212: 2 (2 buys, 0 sells): …", or "No new orders since the previous refresh" / "No change in holdings". A pie purchase shows up as new orders plus new or larger positions. - Every problem and its fix : a key Trading 212 refuses (HTTP 401/403: check live key and Portfolio / Account data permissions), a rate limit (wait a minute, refresh again), an unreadable balance or pie list. A failed call is never silent : the refresh is marked "Finished with problems", nothing wrong is saved (no zero-value snapshot; no snapshot without positions), and the box says the analyses (ratings, strategy, entry, holdings, alerts) used the previous snapshot from <date so they do not include anything bought since. - If only the pie list could not be read, positions are still saved and you are warned that pie grouping may be incomplete.

chunks.text: A fund with under 200 weeks of price history shows no level and the section says how many had none. Listings on the London exchange are quoted in pence (shown as 2,500p, never as pounds); Xetra and Amsterdam in euros; the quote currency from the price history decides, and the live price comes from the same series so level and price are always in the same unit. Not mapped: other exchanges. - Status compares the live price with the zone: Below the zone , In the zone , Approaching the zone (within 3% above), Above the zone , or Live price unavailable . A single-number level ("wait for $150") counts as "in" within 1.5%. - Live price comes from the Entry Analysis rows (value buy scores, native currency, so it is comparable with a USD zone). If it is missing, or in another currency, the card says so; it never guesses. The price the source showed when captured is labelled as a snapshot. - Commentary is generated from the numbers only (distance to the zone, your average cost against the zone, the source's tags). It describes and never instructs; nothing here is advice.

chunks.heading: 0. 💧 Dip Planner (#dip-planner-content, top of the tab)
chunks.text: No fixed budget. You type what you want to invest (or tap £50 / £100 / £200 / £500) and press Plan it . The plan is worked out in the browser from the Entry Analysis rows, your pies and the market mood saved by the last Refresh; nothing is sent anywhere. Module docs/js/dipplan.js (loadDipPlanner, dipPlanRun, pure dpPlanCompute), rolled out to every dashboard. 1. Is it a dip? Strong (full amount used): market mood is Fear or Extreme fear (VIX 20+) or the S&P 500 is 8%+ below its high. Moderate (half used, half kept back): S&P 4–8% down, or 40%+ of your holdings 8%+ below their own highs. Otherwise no dip: the cash is held and the card says so. Tick Plan it even if there is no market dip to see where it would go anyway (labelled as not a dip signal). 2. Score every stock 0–100 from eight signals: RSI 18, Momentum 10, Volume 6, Order flow (estimated) 6, Entry point 20, Dip depth 10, PE ratio 12, Quality score (Entry Analysis) 18. A signal with no data (for example no PE on an ETF) is left out and the rest re-weighted; the stock's chips show "n/a". 3.

chunks.title: 🎯 Strategy
chunks.heading: 0. 💧 Dip Planner (#dip-planner-content, top of the tab)
chunks.text: Decide per stock: 80+ strong buy, 72+ buy, 58+ accumulate, otherwise hold. Overbought (RSI 70+, or RSI 65+ at the 52-week high, or Entry Analysis "hold / avoid") is always hold: no new money. 4. Decide per pie: a pie is INVEST if at least one stock passes and its average score is 50+, otherwise HOLD with the reason. The money is split by buy strength; no pie gets more than 50% (65% when only two pies qualify). Holdings outside any pie are listed as "Not in a pie" and bought directly. 5. Whole pie or custom balance: if the signal-based split is within 15 points of the pie's own target weights, the card says invest in the whole pie ; otherwise custom balance and names the stocks to favour and to skip. Each stock shows its target and current weight in the pie and both amounts (whole-pie £ and custom £). Amounts add up to the penny. 6. Each pie opens to its stocks with signal chips (green / amber / red), the score and the reason. Honesty: prices, RSI, volume, momentum and PE are Yahoo daily data from the last Refresh (the card shows when, and warns after 3 days).

chunks.title: ⚡ Swing (1–10 day trades)
chunks.heading: The one rule that matters
chunks.text: No valid entry = no recommendation. The card says “No entry today” . Nothing is shown as “watch”, “almost” or “wait for”, and doing nothing is a valid answer. Nothing is recommended until the rules have been back-tested : with no passing back-test the tab shows no entries at all, only the reason.

chunks.title: ⚡ Swing (1–10 day trades)
chunks.heading: Universe (what is scanned)
chunks.text: - Your holdings that are not inside a pie (Untagged / Individual) with an Entry Analysis score of 60+ . - Watchlist stocks whose quality label is Good . ETFs, crypto and commodities are left out. - Anything below the quality bar is listed under Not checked , with the reason. Pie holdings are never scanned.

chunks.title: ⚡ Swing (1–10 day trades)
chunks.heading: Entry rules (fixed, not tuned on the data)
chunks.text: All must be true: price above a rising 50-day average · RSI 70 or lower · not stretched far above the 20-day average · average daily turnover over 1 million · daily range 1–6% of price · volume data present (no volume = “cannot verify”, never an entry) · at least 60 daily bars. Then one of two setups: ; Setup ; Needs ; ; Pullback bounce ; RSI fell from 58+ to 35–55 · price at the 20/50-day zone · a green day back up on at least normal volume · room below the recent high for 1.5× the risk ; ; Breakout ; Close above the 20-day high on 1.5× volume , not already more than 1 ATR past the level ;

chunks.title: ⚡ Swing (1–10 day trades)
chunks.heading: Exit plan (shown with every entry)
chunks.text: - Stop: under the last 3 lows (never more than 3 ATR below the price; if it would be, there is no entry). - Target: 2× the risk (2R). - Time exit: the close of day 10 if neither is hit. Entry is skipped if the live price has already run more than half an ATR past the signal, or is through the stop. - Type an amount per trade (no fixed budget) to see shares and the £ at risk to the stop.

chunks.title: ⚡ Swing (1–10 day trades)
chunks.heading: Validation box
chunks.text: Shows the latest back-test: all trades, out-of-sample (most recent 40% of dates, never tuned on) and a random 10-day entry baseline, after a 0.4% round-trip cost, next-day-open entries and stop-before-target. The tab opens its gate only if out-of-sample expectancy is positive , profit factor ≥ 1.2 , there are 150+ trades (40+ out of sample) and it beats the random entry . Re-run weekly and on any rule change by the Swing back-test workflow.

chunks.title: ⚡ Swing (1–10 day trades)
chunks.heading: What it does not do (and says so)
chunks.text: Earnings dates are not checked (avoid holding through results) · the back-test uses today's liquid stocks, so survivorship bias flatters it · the quality screen has no history, so it is not in the back-test · live prices come from Yahoo daily data, refreshed on Scan now .

The demo has no volume candles, so every stock shows “data unverified” there. Tests: tests/zk swing test.mjs (rules, exits, costs, no look-ahead, the gate) · tests/swing layout test.py (360/390px, gate closed / open / no entry).

chunks.title: ⚡ Swing (1–10 day trades)
chunks.heading: 🧪 Paper trading (fake money, under the Swing tab)
chunks.text: A forward test , not a recommendation. You type a weekly amount (there is no default) and two fake accounts get the same deposit every Monday-week: ; Account ; What it does ; ; Trend account ; Buys that amount of a stock when the Minervini trend template + 20-day breakout on 1.5× volume fires on a completed day, filled at the next session's open , up to 5 at a time. Sells at the next open after a close under the 50-day average , at once on a 15% fall , or after 120 days ; ; World ETF (VWRP.L) ; Puts the same deposit into the ETF each week (the bar the trend account must beat) ; - Honest fills: signals use completed bars only; an order is cancelled if the open is above the entry ceiling (price ran away) or through the stop; every buy and sell pays 0.2% . No real money, no orders are ever sent. - Catches up when opened: nothing runs while the app is closed. Missed weeks are credited and the ETF is bought at that week's real open. - Universe: the stocks the Swing tab scans (holdings outside pies and Good-quality watchlist stocks), so it only trades names you have.

Judge after 8–12 weeks and 20+ closed trades . - Stored in the database: the whole account is one JSON value under the key paper in your user ui prefs row (per user, follows your login on the private app; browser-only on the legacy page, like the demo). chunks.text: Three sections (tabs .w-cats): 📈 Stocks · 🛢 Commodities · ₿ Crypto . - Search (any stock or ETF worldwide, e.g. Toyota, 0700.HK; crypto via Yahoo and Trading 212 ETPs; commodities via Trading 212 ETCs and market futures). Each bookmarked item shows this week's call : ; Call ; Meaning ; ; 🟢 ENTER ; Buy this week ; ; 🔵 ACCUMULATE ; Buy in steps ; ; 🟡 HOLD ; Wait for the price points ; ; 🔴 AVOID ; Not this week ; together with price points with £ per step, how much to buy (worked out from the amount you type for that section: there is no fixed budget; with no amount entered the steps show "—"), RSI , volume and quality and an analyst chip (Yahoo Finance recommendation and number of analysts, or "no coverage"; never an invented rating).

chunks.title: ⭐ Watchlist & IPO Watch
chunks.heading: Watchlist
chunks.text: - Order flow (estimated) : each stock card shows a chip (Large buyer / Large seller / Buyers leaning / Sellers leaning / Flow neutral, always marked "est.") and a line in Details. It is inferred from daily candles : volume at least 2.5× the stock's own 20-day average on a wide candle that closes in the top (or bottom) half of its range, within the last 5 sessions, plus 20-day volume-weighted close position. It is not real order flow : Yahoo's free data has no order book, tape or buy/sell split, so "buy orders of 20k lots" cannot be seen, and a fixed lot count would mean nothing across stocks (so the threshold is relative). It can only soften an ENTER to ACCUMULATE (large-seller footprint) or add a supporting line (large-buyer footprint); it never creates a buy and is shown beside, never blended into, the analyst consensus. With no volume or High/Low history it says nothing (unverified). Real block-trade / Level 2 data needs a licensed feed (backlog). - ✕ Remove stops all tracking of that item. - Drag to reorder : every card has a ⠿ handle on its left.
